#### The motivation for this project
As an avid NYC birder, I look through my binoculars each weekend. And what do I see? Pigeons. From a distance, these birds are, at most, a minor nuisance (as they scare away other birds). However, to many people, they are enough of a bother to submit pigeon-related complaints via 311. We were curious to investigate the issues these pigeons cause in the lives of New Yorkers. 

#### The intended final products
We want to describe and analyze pigeon-related complaints in NYC using publicly available data from 311 Complaint Data which feature the word "pigeon." Our project will include static visualizations which characterize complaints by time, location, income level, and building type. We will identify the species of pigeons which are present in NYC using eBird. We also plan to create a dashboard which utilizes the API available via the 311 data source to provide real-time, pigeon-related complaint monitoring. Finally, we will explore factors which may be associated with pigeon-related complaints and  311's response time, including time, building type, location/borough, and socioeconomic factors, such as income.  

#### The anticipated data sources
1) 311 Pigeon Complaint Data. NYC Open Data. https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Social-Services/contains-Pigeon-/iea7-sinw/about_data 
2) EOD – eBird Observation Dataset. Cornell Lab of Ornithology. https://www.gbif.org/dataset/4fa7b334-ce0d-4e88-aaae-2e0c138d049e 
3) Income Data Tables. United States Census Bureau. https://www.census.gov/topics/income-poverty/income/data/tables.html

##### Planned analyses: 
1) Temporal trend of complaints: 16 years of data - Have the number of complaints changed? - Yearly and seasonal trends in the level of complaints.
2) Geographical distribution of complaints: By borough and neighborhood (incorporate income). - Temporal trends of pigeon complaints by borough.
3) Type and details of complaints - Problem: Unsanitary pigeon condition versus trapping pigeon. - Problem detail: Pigeon waste versus pigeon odor.
4) Pigeon complaint by building type - Residential versus commercial building versus, etc. 
5) Brief scientific overview of pigeon species in NYC.
6) Correlations between pigeon sighting location on eBird and where people file pigeon complaints?
7) Use the API and have a dashboard of complaint monitoring.
8) How long it takes for a 311 Pigeon call to get resolved - Overall and by geography and income.

##### Visualizations: 
* Tables, line and bar charts for counts and temporal trends (by location type and neighborhood)
* Histogram for days to resolve complaints faceted by geography or income level
* Maps of pigeon sightings and complaints

##### Potential coding challenges: 
* Amount of pigeon data available (we have 16 years of data, but realistically how many people are submitting pigeon complaints and how representative are those people?)
* Understanding how data are categorized (e.g., pigeon waste versus pigeon odor or 3+ family apartment building versus 3+ family mixed use building).
* Co-locating pigeon species data to NYC using longitude and latitude 
* Working with timestamps for when complaints were opened/closed (e.g., missing closure data).
